content: Globus pharyngis is a condition characterized by a persistent sensation of having phlegm or an obstruction in the throat, despite the absence of any actual physical blockage. The sensation of a lump in the throat associated with globus pharyngis is often attributed to inflammation in specific areas of the throat, such as the larynx or hypopharynx. In some cases, this sensation may also be linked to underlying anxiety disorders. The potential causes of globus pharyngis include anxiety, conversion disorder, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and other psychiatric conditions. It is important to distinguish globus pharyngis from other disorders. Individuals with this condition are able to swallow normally, which differentiates it from true dysphagia. However, the sensation can still be highly bothersome and distressing.
